scenario_scope: Intake of Corben Sorenson's The Regret Engine as a cross-layer conceptual source for decision-time counterfactual comparison, protected learning signals, replay, procedural repair, incident learning, and bounded update governance.

cases.decision_rationale: Each major mechanism has an established owner. Integration should make the handoffs explicit without moving planning, learning, evidence, memory, readiness, or operations authority into one monolithic subsystem chapter.
evidence_transition_preconditions: complete uncertainty, failure, baseline, and cost accounting
promotion_blockers: no local implementation, experiment, reproduction, or formal check
non_claims: does not establish the quality of any counterfactual or causal estimate
does not authorize actor self-adjudication or policy promotion

cases.decision_rationale: A standalone paper-shaped chapter would repeat the Decision Capsule, feedback lease, replay buffer, procedure compiler, evidence ledger, readiness gate, and incident lifecycle already assigned elsewhere. The integrated architecture can show the joined subsystem without duplicating ownership.
required_before_drafting: not applicable; integrate through the established owners
evidence_transition_preconditions: a future implemented tribunal or counterfactual-evaluation service would require fresh boundary adjudication
promotion_blockers: topic breadth and a named subsystem do not create a distinct chapter boundary
non_claims: does not forbid a future chapter if implementation reveals an unowned lifecycle

validation_boundary: Records a full-paper, existing-owner integration and rejects a duplicate chapter. It does not validate the formalism, identify real counterfactuals, reproduce experiments, establish novelty, or move support.
non_claims: does not add a Lean proof target
does not publish the raw paper
does not authorize training, deployment, release, or claim promotion
